subject: Consumer API: heartbeat misses + 502 spike — routing failover request
messages:
From: Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@primecare.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consumer API - elevated 502 rate and missed heartbeats (AZ1)

Hi team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 502s and request timeouts hitting our consumer endpoints around 08:45 PDT. Heartbeat pings from our edge proxies show intermittent misses to AZ1 over the last 30 minutes. Throughput looks steady from our side, but latency for short requests (<=128 tokens) jumped from ~80ms p50 to ~720ms p50.

This is affecting checkout flows for PrimeCare customers — two merchants already reported failed requests and fallback pages. Can you confirm whether this is an AZ-level issue on your side and whether you have a mitigation plan? We need an ETA for stabilization and an estimate of lost successful requests for the last hour.

I've attached a short capture of our proxy logs and a screenshot of the error rate graph. Happy to jump on a 15-minute call.

Thanks,
Amelia Reyes
Head of Platform Ops, PrimeCare AI
amelia.reyes@primecare.ai
attachments: proxy_capture_08-45.json, error_rate_screenshot.png
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@primecare.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consumer API - elevated 502 rate and missed heartbeats (AZ1)

Amelia — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're looking into this as P0.

Immediate steps we are taking:
- Triage: on-call infra is analyzing AZ1 telemetry and request queues (David is leading).
- Short-term mitigation: proposing a small cross-region traffic shift (5-10%) from AZ1 -> USW2 to reduce queue pressure while we root-caused.
- Communication: will confirm a remediation ETA in the next 20 minutes and keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

Could you share whether PrimeCare has any routing constraints (data residency / legal) for this traffic? If so, mention it now — it may affect our ability to shift traffic.

I'll follow up with a technical snapshot and a proposed traffic-shift plan.

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0124
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@primecare.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consumer API - elevated 502 rate and missed heartbeats (AZ1)

Amelia / Rohan — quick technical summary from the runtime team:

What we observe now:
- 08:40-09:10 PDT: AZ1 serving fleet shows a sharp increase in KV-cache eviction rate and sustained queue depth on the smallest-latency pool (short seq len, small-batch path).
- Error profile: 502 gateway errors map to per-node overload responses when kernel busy time exceeds thresholds; not a networking partition.
- Correlation: concurrent rollout of model-variant v3q woke up a heavier kernel path that increases per-token compute for short requests; combined with a spike in small-batch requests this saturates a subset of AZ1 nodes.

Immediate recommendation (risk-mitigated):
1) Steer 7% of traffic for the consumer route to USW2 (compatible model variant available) for 30 minutes to relieve pressure.
2) Spin up 4 temporary burst VMs in USW2 with quantized variant (will add negligible cold-start latency).
3) Revert the v3q rollout in AZ1 (can be rolled back in 8 minutes).

Attached: netlogs_az1-20280521.zip and slo_snapshot-20280521.csv.

Risk notes: steering requires authorization for cross-region routing for PrimeCare (I see contractual mention of US-only but not region-locked; confirm). Also we should pre-authorize a one-time burst capacity charge for USW2.

If we get authorization now, infra can enact the 7% steer in ~6 minutes and the bank of burst VMs in ~9 minutes.

—David
David Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
From: Amelia Reyes <amelia.reyes@primecare.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@primecare.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consumer API - elevated 502 rate and missed heartbeats (AZ1)

Thanks — that summary is helpful. PrimeCare has a US-region requirement but not an AZ-only restriction; steering to USW2 is acceptable. We do have a pre-approved spend cap for emergency bursts; please proceed and keep us posted on the charge.

We also need an impact estimate for the last 45 minutes (approx number of failed requests and % of checkout attempts impacted). We'd prefer a short postmortem within 24 hours.

One other ask: given this caused visible customer outages, PrimeCare will request a one-time credit for the affected window. I will open a support billing case now (I can include your SRE notes).

Appreciate the quick response.

—Amelia
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Consumer API - elevated 502 rate and missed heartbeats (AZ1) — exec ask

Forwarding the thread for visibility and urgent approval. TL;DR: PrimeCare (large strategic customer, PC-4382) experienced an AZ1 localized overload tied to a v3q model variant rollout + sudden small-batch traffic spike. David recommends a short 7% steer to USW2 + burst capacity and rollback of the variant. Customer has authorized cross-region steering and pre-approved emergency spend.

Ask for Execs: please approve the one-time capacity burst (estimated incremental cost $3,600 for the surge window) and sign-off on a goodwill credit for PrimeCare. Proposed customer comms and a draft credit figure are attached in proposed_traffic_shift_plan.pdf.
